title: Reliability Partner Orchestration Bootcamp — 90-Day Activation Plan
content:
Purpose:
This is a pragmatic, execution-oriented bootcamp plan to accelerate cross-functional adoption of the reliability program and service-level objectives (SLOs) for Q2 2026. The goal is to create repeatable onboarding, align measurement definitions, and deliver a small set of stabilized SLOs for priority services within 90 days.

Audience and scope:
- Primary: SREs, platform engineers, product/feature owners, service leads, and solutions engineering partners.
- Scope: 6 target services (mix of hosted-api, dedicated, and private deployment surfaces), SLO definitions, dashboards, runbook handoff, and first-run incident simulations.

Success criteria (measurable):
- 6 services have production SLOs instrumented, dashboarded, and alerted (objective: 3 in 45 days, all 6 in 90 days).
- Error budget burn rate thresholds established and tested via at least one tabletop per service.
- On-call runbook link added to each service repo and validated with a post-exercise checklist.
- Cross-org playbook (1 page) published and accepted by product and platform leadership.

High-level approach and phases (90 days):
Phase 0 — Pre-bootcamp (Week -2 to 0): intake + alignment
- Collect service intake forms (owner, traffic profile, current SLO-like signals). Jira: SRE-4523 is the intake epic.
- Quick tech discovery calls (30m) per service to confirm export points and telemetry.
- Ship a lightweight instrumentation template and Grafana dashboard seed.

Phase 1 — Bootcamp Launch (Weeks 1–2): collocated kickoff and labs
Week 1:
- Day 1: Opening — goals, definitions (latency SLO vs availability SLO vs quality), risk appetite calibration exercise with product.
- Day 2: Telemetry lab — setting up metrics exporters, prefix/KV cache signal for model-serving paths, and synthetic check probes.
- Day 3: SLO drafting workshop — owners draft SLOs using the standardized rubric (objective, SLIs, measurement window, burn policy).
- Deliverable: draft SLOs committed to git for peer review.

Week 2:
- Embedded pairing sessions: SREs pair with service owners to wire dashboards and basic alerts.
- Runbook template filling and initial incident playbook creation.
- Canary/rollback policy alignment for model-serving rollouts.
- Deliverable: dashboards pointing at production metrics (seeded panels), runbook URL, and issues for remaining telemetry gaps.

Phase 2 — Stabilize & Test (Weeks 3–8): iterate and simulate
Weeks 3–6:
- Implement fixes for telemetry gaps, iterate on SLO thresholds using historical data and synthetic tests.
- Start incremental rollout of alerts (low-noise alerting first).
- Conduct one tabletop incident per service to exercise runbooks and SLO-triggered remediation.
Weeks 7–8:
- Capture lessons, reduce false positives, and finalize alert routing (who gets paged at 2% burn vs 10% burn).
- Deliverable: final SLO doc per service and pager routing configured.

Phase 3 — Handoff & Operationalization (Weeks 9–13): embed and scale
- Handoff artifact pack: SLO definition, dashboard link, runbook, incident postmortem template, and onboarding checklist.
- Cross-team review and leadership sign-off; measure readiness via a short checklist.
- Create a rolling schedule for SLO retros (quarterly).
- Deliverable: signed SLO acceptance and scheduled cadence for retros.

Roles and responsibilities (short):
- Bootcamp lead (owner): Aisha Patel — program cadence, cross-org coordination, reporting.
- SRE pairing leads: Liam Chen, María Gómez — telemetry fixes, dashboard templates, exercises.
- Product liaisons: one per service (named in intake).
- Platform eng: integration work for Dedicated/private deployment telemetry hooks.
- Solutions engineering: customer-facing implications and support readiness.

Artifacts to produce (minimum viable):
- Per-service SLO doc (markdown file in service repo) with acceptance checklist.
- Shared Grafana dashboard templates (seed panels + variables).
- Runbook template and one validated runbook per service.
- Short internal playbook: "When an SLO is burning: 5 steps for the first 30 minutes."
- Heatmap of dependencies mapping (data store, model-serving pool, network egress, third-party services).

Communication and cadence:
- Weekly stakeholders sync (30m) — progress review vs milestones; owner: Aisha.
- Twice-weekly office hours (drop-in) for pairing and instrumentation help.
- Dedicated Slack channel: #reliability-bootcamp (use threads for each service).
- Mid-bootcamp demo day (end of Week 6) for leadership and product stakeholders.

Risk register and mitigations (top items):
- Risk: telemetry gaps in private deployments (on-prem agents or restricted egress).
  Mitigation: pre-provide a lightweight collector container and offline ingestion plan; escalate to platform engineering in Week 0.
- Risk: noisy alerts and alert fatigue.
  Mitigation: conservative alert thresholds, staged rollouts, and a 2-week quiet window to tune.
- Risk: model behavior quality drift not captured by latency-based SLIs.
  Mitigation: include quality SLIs where applicable (e.g., fallback rate, hallucination proxy) and link to Redwood Optimize experiments.

Decision log (examples during bootcamp):
- Decision: default SLO measurement window = 28 days for availability SLOs; agreed Week 1.
- Decision: error budget policy = automatic paging at 10% burn in 1h and ops notification at 5% burn in 24h; pilot services only.

Runbook quick-check template (for validation):
- Does runbook list on-call and primary triage steps? (Y/N)
- Can a new engineer follow it in <15 minutes? (Y/N + notes)
- Is the dashboard linked and does it surface the SLI panels? (Y/N)
- Post-exercise review scheduled? (date)

Scripting and automation suggestions (engineering to-do):
- One-click dashboard seeding script (grafana-cli + templating).
- CI job that validates SLO doc presence and basic linting on PRs.
- Small synthetic harness to exercise model-serving end-to-end and report SLI values daily.

Workshop schedule (example first month):
- Week 1: Kickoff + SLO drafting + telemetry lab (full days; collocated).
- Week 2: Pairing and dashboard wiring (half days + office hours).
- Week 4: Tabletop simulations (one per service across two days).

Post-bootcamp follow-up (30/60/90 checklist):
- 30 days: confirm dashboards stable and one postmortem ran if error budget exceeded.
- 60 days: assess SLO utility across product decisions (did teams use SLOs to influence rollout or throttling?).
- 90 days: leadership review; catalog wins and define next cohort for additional services.

Open questions (to resolve in Week 0 kickoff):
- Which services will be in the initial cohort (product leads to confirm by intake deadline)?
- How will we measure quality SLI signals for model outputs (suggested proxies: reranks, fallback counts, customer rate-limiting errors)?
- Are there regulatory constraints for telemetry export in any private deployments?

Immediate next actions (this week):
- Publish intake form and assign owners (Aisha). (JIRA: SRE-4523)
- Schedule kickoff week and block calendar for pairing leads.
- Prepare Grafana dashboard seed and instrumentation checklist.

Notes to reviewers: this is intentionally pragmatic and low-friction; the plan prioritizes fast wins that are repeatable. Expect to iterate on the SLO rubric and instrumentation templates after the first cohort completes Week 6 demos.

Appendix: Useful links and templates
- Dashboard seed repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability-templates
- Runbook template: confluence:runbook-template-v2
- Intake form (draft): https://forms.redwood.com/sre-bootcamp-intake
- Related tickets: JIRA:SRE-4523 (intake), JIRA:SRE-4590 (automation), GitHub PR 87 (dashboard seed)

-- End of bootcamp plan (draft) --
